raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Apply EP weight filtering before InstantTensor I/O using scitix/InstantTensor#29, released in InstantTensor 0.2.2.

Skip non-local expert payloads while retaining scales, shared experts, and fused tensors. Keep collective loading for checkpoints without filterable expert weights, and match checkpoint names literally.

#58016 covers the standard safetensors reader; this change reuses its EP predicate for InstantTensor.

<details>
<summary>Pull Request Checklist</summary>

- [x] Used `/pr-checklist`.
- [x] Design fit.
- [x] Testing and validation; performance limitation noted below.
- [x] Code quality and style.
- [x] Pull request contents.

</details>

## Tests

InstantTensor 0.2.2, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130.

- 1 × NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3: `../.venv/bin/python -m pytest --noconftest -q tests/model_executor/model_loader/instanttensor_loader/test_weight_utils.py tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_ep_weight_filter.py -k 'not test_instanttensor_model_loader'` — 41 passed.
- Earlier validation of the unchanged production fix on 2 × H100: native two-rank reader checks passed; tiny Qwen2MoE at TP=2/EP=2 produced identical tokens and top-5 logprobs to safetensors.

Pre-commit and Linux-target mypy passed. EP=8 loading performance remains unbenchmarked; the separate PyTorch 2.15 nightly NCCL2 incompatibility remains.

`tensor_filter` doesn't exist in instanttensor 0.1.9, and the pin is still `>= 0.1.9` (setup.py, requirements/cuda.txt). So `--load-format instanttensor --enable-ep-weight-filter`, which loads fine today without filtering, would raise a `TypeError` in `safe_open`. The new test mocks `instanttensor`, so CI won't catch it. Bump the pin to the release that includes InstantTensor#29 in this PR, or check `inspect.signature(instanttensor.safe_open)` and fall back to the unfiltered path.

nodes.body: This turns off NCCL loading whenever EP filtering is enabled, even when the filter keeps every tensor. On fused-expert checkpoints (e.g. GPT-OSS), `parse_expert_id` returns None for every name, so nothing is skipped, but every rank still reads the full model from storage on its own (about 8x the storage reads at EP=8). Only drop the process group when the filter actually skips something, e.g. by checking the names in `model.safetensors.index.json` first.

The scale tensors kept for non-local experts also sit between skipped weights, so each becomes its own tiny read (for FP8 DeepSeek-V3, tens of thousands per rank). Together this can make the filtered load slower than the unfiltered NCCL load, and multi-GPU EP is untested. Could you benchmark a real EP=8 load against the current path before merging?

+def test_instanttensor_ep_collective_loading(
+    monkeypatch, tmp_path, weight_name, local_ids, collective
+):
+    """Keep fused checkpoints collective and expert decisions rank-independent."""
+    from vllm.model_executor.model_loader import weight_utils
+
+    path = tmp_path / "model.safetensors"
+    save_file({weight_name: torch.ones(1)}, str(path))
+    native_open = MagicMock()
+    reader = native_open.return_value.__enter__.return_value
+    reader.total_tensor_size = 0
+    reader.tensors.return_value = ()
+    monkeypatch.setitem(
+        sys.modules, "instanttensor", SimpleNamespace(safe_open=native_open)
+    )
+    group = SimpleNamespace(world_size=2, device_group=object())
+    monkeypatch.setattr(weight_utils, "get_world_group", lambda: group)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(current_platform, "is_cuda", lambda: True)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(current_platform, "current_device", lambda: 0)
+    list(instanttensor_weights_iterator([str(path)], False, local_expert_ids=local_ids))
+    kwargs = native_open.call_args.kwargs
+    assert kwargs["process_group"] is (group.device_group if collective else None)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(

+)

+        "model.layers[0].attn.weight": torch.ones(2),

+    loaded = dict(

+    )
+    del weights["mlp.experts.1.gate_proj.weight"]
+    assert loaded.keys() == weights.keys()
+    for name, tensor in loaded.items():
+        torch.testing.assert_close(tensor.cpu(), weights[name], rtol=0, atol=0)
+
